transcriptionNote: All 150 numbered questions and four options have been checked against the uploaded source scan, including the dice/triangle figures and mathematical notation. All 150 questions have an independently solved answer and explanation. The source PDF did not include an official answer key; ambiguous items are flagged in answerStatus.

questions.text: He ambled towards his brother and whispered something.
questions.explanation: “Ambled” means walked slowly and without hurry. “Strolled” has the same sense of walking in a relaxed, unhurried way. “Leaned”, “bent” and “stooped” describe changes in body position, not the manner of walking. Therefore, option D is the closest synonym.
questions.sectionInstruction: Direction (Q. Nos. 1–10): In these sentences, out of the four alternatives given, choose the one which best expresses the meaning of the word in italics.

questions.text: The sweet smell of mangoes attracted bees and birds which flocked around them.
questions.explanation: When bees and birds “flocked around” the mangoes, they gathered there in a group. “Congregated” also means came together or assembled in one place. “Converged” means moved towards a common point, which is close but less exact; “covered” and “assimilated” do not fit. Option A is best.

questions.text: We arrived at a conclusion that there was a paucity of raw materials.
questions.explanation: “Paucity” is a noun meaning a very small quantity or shortage. “Scarcity” has the same meaning, so option C is correct. “Abundance” and “availability” suggest that something is plentiful or obtainable, which is the opposite idea.

questions.text: After the battle was over, the soldier was accused of perfidy.
questions.explanation: “Perfidy” means deliberate betrayal, treachery or breach of faith. “Treason” is betrayal of one's country or sovereign, so it is the closest available synonym in this set. “Heresy” concerns beliefs, “fallacy” is a mistaken idea, and “cowardice” is lack of courage. Option A is the best match.

questions.text: My father had always been an adorable man.
questions.explanation: “Adorable” describes someone or something very lovable and delightful. Among the four choices, “delightful” is the closest in meaning. “Amiable” means friendly or pleasant in manner, “upright” means honest, and “admirable” means worthy of respect. Option C is the best fit, although the choices are not exact synonyms.

questions.text: The Chairperson admonished the Secretary.
questions.explanation: To “admonish” someone is to warn, reprimand or correct that person firmly for something. “Warned” is therefore the closest option. “Administered” means managed or gave something, “advised” is generally softer guidance, and “appointed” means assigned to a position. Option B is best.

questions.text: They talked about India's economic security ____ global recession.
questions.explanation: “Vis-à-vis” is a French expression used in English to mean in relation to, with regard to, or in comparison with. In the sentence, India's economic security is being discussed in relation to the global recession. Option A is correct.

questions.text: There was opulence in the farm when the farmer's son had joined the farm.
questions.explanation: “Opulence” means great wealth, richness or luxurious abundance. “Wealth” is the direct closest meaning among the choices, so option B is correct. “Prosperity” is a related condition of success or well-being, but “wealth” is the more direct synonym.

questions.text: I was too tired of his puerile behavior.
questions.explanation: “Puerile” means childish, immature or characteristic of a child, especially when describing behaviour that is silly or not sensible. “Immature” is the closest synonym. “Premature” means happening too early, “gibberish” is meaningless speech, and “notorious” means widely known for something bad. Option A is correct.

questions.text: My mother had always guided me with sufficient prudence.
questions.explanation: “Prudence” means the quality of making careful, sensible decisions after considering possible consequences. “Caution” is the closest option because a prudent person acts carefully and avoids unnecessary risks. “Patience”, “persistence” and “surety” have different meanings. Option B is correct.

questions.text: She is not reflecting any kind of perseverance in this matter.
questions.explanation: The instruction for Q11–Q20 asks for the opposite meaning. “Perseverance” means continuing with determination despite difficulty. “Vacillation” means repeatedly wavering or changing one's mind, showing a lack of firmness. It is the best opposite among the choices, so option A is correct.
questions.sectionInstruction: Direction (Q. Nos. 11–20): In these sentences, out of the four alternatives given, choose the one which is opposite in meaning of the word in italics.

questions.text: Man has a surplus of knowledge that animals lack.
questions.explanation: The instruction asks for an antonym. “Surplus” means an amount greater than what is needed; “dearth” means a shortage or lack. These meanings are opposites, so option A is correct. “Excess” is actually a synonym of surplus.

questions.text: They are the contemporary poets emerging in the latest anthologies.
questions.explanation: “Contemporary” means belonging to the present time or the same period. “Old-fashioned” is the intended opposite and is the best available choice (A). However, “antiquated” (B) also means old-fashioned or outdated, so the question contains two plausible opposites and should be treated as ambiguous unless an official key confirms the examiner's intended choice.

questions.text: There are certain new methods of solving these problems.
questions.explanation: The word marked in the source is “solving”. “Solving” means finding an answer or working out a problem. “Complicating” means making something more difficult or complex, which is the closest contrasting idea among the four options. The wording is not a precise antonym pair, so option A is a best-fit answer rather than an exact opposite.

questions.text: We all have vowed to abide by the rules of the organization.
questions.explanation: The target word is “vowed”, which means made a solemn promise or pledge. “Renounced” means formally gave up, rejected or abandoned something, making it the closest opposite among the options. “Disclaimed” can also mean denied a claim or responsibility, so the choice is based on the sense of withdrawing a commitment. Option C is the best fit.

questions.text: She is tired of the frequent visits from her relatives.
questions.explanation: “Frequent” means happening often or at short intervals. “Occasional” means happening from time to time, but not regularly or often. These meanings contrast, so option D is correct. “Moderate” means average or not extreme; it is not the opposite of frequent.

questions.text: Raima has never claimed any share of the property for herself.
questions.explanation: To “claim” a share of property is to assert that one has a right to receive it. To “disclaim” is to deny, renounce or refuse such a claim. Therefore, “disclaimed” is the closest opposite in this sentence and option B is correct.

questions.text: He is much apprehensive about his reputation.
questions.explanation: “Apprehensive” means anxious, uneasy or worried about something that may happen. “Unconcerned” means not worried or not troubled, so it expresses the opposite meaning. Option A is correct. “Comprehensive” means complete, while “rudderless” means lacking direction.

questions.text: I am not going to pacify anybody even if they do not agree.
questions.explanation: To “pacify” someone is to calm that person or reduce anger and hostility. “Aggravate” means make a problem or feeling worse or more intense, which is the opposite direction. Option B is correct.

questions.text: She is as self-complacent as her brother.
questions.explanation: “Self-complacent” describes someone who is smug or excessively satisfied with themselves. “Demure” describes a modest, reserved or quiet manner, making it the closest contrasting option in this set. The contrast is not exact—“humble” would be a clearer antonym—but option B is the best available choice.

questions.text: We are delighted to go ____ a trip to France.
questions.explanation: The fixed English expression is “go on a trip”. We use “on” with the noun “trip” to describe taking a journey or holiday: “They went on a trip to France.” “Go to a trip”, “go in a trip” and “go down a trip” are not standard constructions in this context. Therefore, option B is correct.

questions.text: At the dawn of history, India started ____ her unending quest.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses the expression “start on a quest”, meaning begin a search or a long effort to achieve something. “On” is the preposition conventionally used with “quest” in this construction. The other options do not form the intended phrase. Therefore, option C is correct.

questions.text: He resides in a small hut ____ the river.
questions.explanation: The preposition “by” can mean beside or close to something. A hut “by the river” is a hut situated near the river. “Over” means above or across; “before” indicates earlier or in front of; and “around” means surrounding. Option A gives the intended location.

questions.text: They became indignant ____ the living images that the prosperous tradesmen had projected.
questions.explanation: “Indignant” means feeling anger because something is unjust or offensive. The common construction is “indignant over” something, as in “indignant over the decision”. “For”, “on” and “under” do not fit this sentence's intended prepositional phrase. Option C is correct.

questions.text: The epidemic had broken ____ in the village quite fast.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb “break out” means begin suddenly, especially of a disease, fire, war or disturbance. Thus, “the epidemic had broken out” means the epidemic had begun or spread in the village. “Break up” means separate or end; the other options do not form the required expression. Option D is correct.

questions.text: She has been putting ____ weight since I met her for the first time.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb “put on weight” means gain weight. The sentence describes a change in the person's body weight since the speaker first met her. “Put in”, “put up” and “put off” have different meanings and cannot be used in this expression. Option A is correct.

questions.text: He has been chafed enough ____ her authoritative gaze.
questions.explanation: The expression “chafe under” means feel irritated, frustrated or resentful because of someone's control, restrictions or authority. The sentence says he has become irritated under her authoritative gaze. “Below”, “at” and “in” do not complete this idiom naturally. Option A is correct.

questions.text: She has jumped ____ the conclusion without bothering to know the whole story.
questions.explanation: The fixed idiom is “jump to a conclusion”. It means form an opinion or make a decision too quickly without knowing all the facts. “Jump into” is used in other contexts, but not in this idiom. Therefore, option C is correct.

questions.text: Richie has gone ____ for fishing.
questions.explanation: “Go out for fishing” means leave one's present place in order to fish. The word “out” expresses movement away from the current location. “Go by”, “go up” and “go through” have different meanings and do not complete this sentence naturally. Option B is the intended answer.

questions.text: The cat had jumped ____ the tin roof as it was very hot.
questions.explanation: “Onto” expresses movement from one place to a surface. The cat moved and landed on the tin roof, so “jumped onto the tin roof” is the correct construction. “Into” suggests entering an enclosed space, while “off” means away from a surface. Option B is correct.

questions.text: I can get an eagle's eye view from this part of the building.
options: picture from high up in the sky
questions.explanation: An “eagle's-eye view” is a very clear, keen or comprehensive view. The closest option in this question is “sharp view” (C). A view from high in the sky is more literally a “bird's-eye view”, but that is not the same expression asked here. Thus, option C is the best match.

questions.text: She has just delivered her maiden speech.
questions.explanation: A “maiden speech” is the first formal speech a person gives in a particular assembly or role. “Debut” also means a first appearance or performance, so “debut speech” is the closest option. The other choices describe the quality or strength of a speech, not whether it is the person's first. Option A is correct.

questions.text: His son had gone to sea.
questions.explanation: The expression “go to sea” traditionally means take up work as a sailor or begin a seafaring life. It does not simply mean travel to the seaside. Therefore, “become a sailor” is the correct interpretation, option B.

questions.text: The agenda is under the carpet.
questions.explanation: The expression “sweep something under the carpet” means conceal or hide a problem rather than deal with it openly. The sentence's “under the carpet” conveys the idea of something hidden. “Under discussion” and “neglected” do not express the idiom's central meaning. Option A is the closest answer.

questions.text: The student has walked after his teacher.
questions.explanation: In this question, “walked after his teacher” is intended to mean followed the teacher's example or copied the teacher's conduct. “Imitated” means copied someone's actions or manner, so option B is the intended choice. The sentence is somewhat awkwardly phrased; “followed his teacher's example” would be clearer English.

questions.text: The young girl is trying her best to reach the zenith.
options: to climb up to the peak
questions.explanation: “Zenith” means the highest point or peak. In a figurative sense, it can mean the greatest level of success, fame or achievement. “To achieve the highest glory” expresses that figurative meaning more accurately than physically climbing stairs or reaching a terrace. Option C is correct.

questions.text: She is out and out an ambitious woman.
questions.explanation: The idiom “out and out” means completely, entirely or thoroughly. In the sentence, it emphasises that she is completely ambitious. “Absolutely” is therefore the closest synonym. The other choices do not convey the idea of completeness. Option A is correct.

questions.text: The tomatoes are dime a dozen in the vegetable market.
questions.explanation: The idiom “a dime a dozen” describes something very common, plentiful and not particularly rare or valuable. The sentence means tomatoes are easily found in the vegetable market. “Very commonly found” is the matching meaning, so option A is correct.

questions.text: The old man had to survive on bread and water.
questions.explanation: “Bread and water” in this context refers to a very basic, limited or meagre diet. The sentence says the old man had to survive with only the bare minimum of food. “Meagre food” is the closest option. It does not mean rich, specially prescribed or necessarily healthy food. Option A is correct.

questions.text: At the end of the day, he is the one who has stirred up the hornet's nest.
questions.explanation: To “stir up a hornet's nest” is an idiom meaning cause trouble, provoke anger or create a difficult situation by doing or saying something. The sentence says he was responsible for creating the problem. Therefore, “caused trouble” (A) is the correct meaning.

questions.text: It has been raining cats and dogs since last Monday.
questions.explanation: “Raining cats and dogs” is an idiom meaning raining very heavily. It does not refer to regularity or habit; it describes the intensity of the rain. Therefore, option B, “raining very heavily”, is correct.

questions.text: My mother had called all and sundry for the party.
options: all the members of the assembly
questions.explanation: “All and sundry” means everybody or all kinds of people, without making a distinction. The mother invited everyone to the party. “Everyone” is the direct meaning, so option C is correct.

questions.text: The student turned into a deer in headlights when she was found cheating in the examination hall.
options: to be caught in a state of bewilderment
to be caught in a wrong position
to be in a mischievous position
questions.explanation: The expression “a deer in the headlights” describes someone who becomes suddenly frozen, stunned or unable to react because of shock or fear. The student is caught by surprise when found cheating. Option A, “caught in a state of bewilderment”, is the closest interpretation.

questions.text: Riya is determined not to beat around the bush while narrating what has happened.
options: talk about many unimportant and confusing things
questions.explanation: “Beat around the bush” means avoid speaking directly about the main subject by talking indirectly or about unimportant details. Option C gives the meaning of the idiom. Because the sentence says “not to beat around the bush”, Riya intends to speak directly rather than ramble. The option defines the idiom itself, so C is the intended answer.

questions.text: I used to go to the market once in a blue moon.
questions.explanation: “Once in a blue moon” means very rarely or at long intervals. “Occasionally” is the closest option among those given, although “very rarely” would be a more exact definition. It does not mean every month or every fifteen days. Option A is correct.

questions.text: She has been residing in this locality for the last four years.
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. “Has been residing” is the present perfect continuous tense, which describes an activity or state that began in the past and continues to the present. “For the last four years” correctly indicates the duration. No segment contains a clear grammatical error, so option D (“No error”) is correct.

questions.text: I wanted a little more than what I have got.
questions.explanation: The sentence can be understood as a comparison between what the speaker wanted in the past and what the speaker has obtained up to the present. “I have got” is present perfect and can refer to the present result. Although a different wording might sound smoother in some contexts, the sentence is acceptable as printed; option D (“No error”) is the best answer.

questions.text: When I reached the house, she had danced in the drawing room.
questions.explanation: The past perfect “had danced” normally describes an action completed before another past event. In this sentence, the intended meaning is that she was in the middle of dancing when the speaker arrived. The natural correction is “she was dancing in the drawing room”. Therefore, segment B contains the error, option B.

questions.text: The effect of all these the world was soothing.
questions.explanation: The standard construction is “the effect of something on something”. The sentence should read: “The effect of all these on the world was soothing.” The preposition “on” is missing between “these” and “the world”, so the error is in segment B. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Simply draw out a sample pattern on the layout plan.
questions.explanation: The instruction asks whether any part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect. “Draw out a sample pattern” can mean prepare or produce a sample design, and “on the layout plan” is an understandable location for that design. No clear grammatical error appears in the printed sentence, so option D (“No error”) is the intended answer.

questions.text: The sum of the present ages of a son and his father is 60 years. Six years ago, father's age was five times the age of the son. After 6 years, what will be the son's age?
questions.explanation: Let the father's present age be F and the son's present age be S. Their present ages add to 60: F+S=60. Six years ago, F−6=5(S−6). Substituting F=60−S gives 60−S−6=5S−30, so 84=6S and S=14. After six years the son will be 14+6=20 years old. Option A is correct.

questions.text: In one hour, a boat goes 14 km/hr along the stream and 8 km/hr against the stream. The speed of the boat in still water is
questions.explanation: A boat's downstream speed equals its still-water speed plus stream speed; its upstream speed equals still-water speed minus stream speed. When we add the two speeds, the stream's effect cancels. Still-water speed = (14+8)÷2 = 22÷2 = 11 km/h. Option B is correct.

questions.text: How many times in a day are the hands of a clock in a straight line but opposite in direction?
questions.explanation: The minute and hour hands are exactly opposite when the angle between them is 180°. This happens 11 times in every 12-hour period (not 12 times, because the hands' relative positions repeat after each hour but do not produce 12 separate opposite positions). A full day has two 12-hour periods, so the number is 11×2=22. Option B is correct.

questions.text: The angle between the minute hand and the hour hand of a clock, when the time is 8:30, is
questions.explanation: At 8:30, the minute hand points at 6, which is 180° from 12. The hour hand moves 30° per hour and 0.5° per minute: 8×30+30×0.5=255°. The difference is 255°−180°=75°. This is already the smaller angle, so option A is correct.

questions.text: A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B can do it in 15 days. They work together for 5 days and the rest of the work is finished by C in two more days. If they got ₹6,000 as wages for the whole work, then find the daily wages of A, B and C.
questions.explanation: A's one-day work rate is 1/10 and B's is 1/15. Together they complete 1/10+1/15=1/6 of the work per day. In five days they complete 5/6, leaving 1/6 for C. C completes that remaining 1/6 in two days, so C's daily rate is 1/12. The daily work-rate ratio is 1/10:1/15:1/12 = 6:4:5. If the daily wages are ₹600, ₹400 and ₹500 respectively, the total paid is A: 5×600=₹3,000; B: 5×400=₹2,000; C: 2×500=₹1,000. Total = ₹6,000, matching the question. Thus option A gives the daily wages.

questions.text: If A:B:C = 2:3:4, then the ratio A/B : B/C : C/A will be
questions.explanation: Given A:B:C=2:3:4, take A=2, B=3 and C=4. Then A/B=2/3, B/C=3/4 and C/A=4/2. To express these as a whole-number ratio, multiply each by the LCM of the denominators, 12: 8:9:24. Option C is correct.

questions.text: A train moving at a speed of 90 km/hr crosses a pole in 7 seconds. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanation: When a train crosses a pole, it travels a distance equal to its own length. Convert 90 km/h to metres per second: 90×1000÷3600=25 m/s. In 7 seconds, distance = speed×time = 25×7=175 metres. Therefore, the train is 175 m long, option C.

questions.text: The positions of dice are given below. Identify the number at the bottom when the top is 5.
questions.explanation: In a standard six-faced die, opposite faces do not touch in any view. Comparing the four arrangements in the source figure, the opposite pairs are 3–6, 1–2 and 4–5. Since 5 is on the top, its opposite face, 4, must be at the bottom. Option D is correct.
questions.diagramDescription: The four dice views show (top, left face, right face): (4, 3, 2), (3, 1, 5), (1, 4, 6), and (2, 3, 5).

questions.text: Find the number of triangles in the given figure.
questions.explanation: The question depends on counting every triangle in the printed diagram, including the smallest triangles and larger triangles formed by combining smaller regions. Count each distinct triangular outline once, working from the smallest regions to the composite shapes and finally the outer triangle. The total in the source figure is 18, so option D is selected. This answer should be checked against the original figure during the final visual audit because a diagram transcription error would change the count.

questions.text: In a row of girls, Alisha and Cinthya occupy the ninth place from the right end and tenth place from the left end, respectively. If they interchange their places, then Alisha and Cinthya occupy seventeenth place from the right and eighteenth place from the left respectively. How many girls are there in the row?
questions.explanation: After Alisha and Cinthya exchange places, Alisha takes Cinthya's original position, which was 10th from the left. She is then 17th from the right. For a person counted from both ends, total number = left rank + right rank − 1. Therefore, total girls = 10+17−1=26. Option A is correct.

questions.text: A is the mother of B. B is the sister of C. D is the son of C. E is the brother of D. F is the mother of E. G is the granddaughter of A. H has only two children B and C. How is F related to H?
questions.explanation: A is the mother of B, and B and C are siblings, so A is also C's mother. D is C's son, and E is D's brother; F is E's mother, so F is also the mother of D and is C's wife. H has only two children, B and C, so C is H's child. Therefore, F is H's daughter-in-law. Option B is correct. The extra statement about G does not affect the required relationship.

questions.text: Z is shorter than Y but taller than X. W is shorter than Z but taller than X and V is shorter than Y but taller than Z. The shortest person is
questions.explanation: The statements give these comparisons: Y>Z>X; also Z>W>X; and V>Z while Y>V. The key fact is that X is shorter than Z and also shorter than W. Since W is taller than X and Z is taller than X, while V is taller than Z, none of the other people is below X. Therefore X is the shortest. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Zara is 6 ranks ahead of Anokhi in a class of 42 students. If Anokhi's rank is eighteenth from the last, then what is Zara's rank from the start?
questions.explanation: Anokhi is 18th from the last in a class of 42. Her rank from the start is 42−18+1=25th. Zara is six places ahead, so her rank is 25−6=19th from the start. Option B is correct.

questions.text: The value of 40 coins of 10 paisa and 20 paisa is ₹5.50. The number of 20 paisa coins is
questions.explanation: Let x be the number of 10-paisa coins and y the number of 20-paisa coins. There are 40 coins, so x+y=40. Their total value is ₹5.50=550 paise, so 10x+20y=550. Divide the value equation by 10: x+2y=55. Subtract x+y=40 to get y=15. Thus there are 15 twenty-paisa coins, option A.

questions.text: In an examination, a student scores 4 marks for every correct answer and loses 1 mark for every wrong answer. If he attempts all 90 questions and secures 140 marks, the number of questions he attempts correctly is
questions.explanation: Let c be the number of correct answers and w the number of wrong answers. All 90 questions are attempted, so c+w=90. The score is 4 for each correct and −1 for each wrong: 4c−w=140. Substitute w=90−c: 4c−(90−c)=140, so 5c=230 and c=46. Option D is correct.

questions.text: If rain is called water, water is called air, air is called cloud, cloud is called sky, sky is called sea, and sea is called road, where do the airplanes fly?
questions.explanation: The question changes the names of things. In reality, aeroplanes fly in the sky. The code says that the word “sky” is called “sea”. Therefore, under the given naming rule, the answer must be “Sea”, option C. Do not confuse the real object with the substituted code word.

questions.text: Robert walks 30 meters in the north direction, after that he takes a right turn and walks 40 meters. After that he takes a right turn and walks 40 meters more and finally he takes a right turn and stops after walking 40 meters. Find the distance of Robert from the initial position.
questions.explanation: Track each movement on a simple north-east-south-west grid. Robert walks 30 m north, 40 m east, 40 m south and 40 m west. The east and west movements cancel. The southward movement is 40 m, which exceeds the 30 m northward movement by 10 m. He finishes 10 m south of the starting point, so the distance is 10 m. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Shobha was facing East. She walked 20 meters. Turning left, she moved 15 meters and then turning right, moved 25 meters. Finally, she turned right and moved 15 meters more. How far is she from her starting point?
questions.explanation: Shobha starts facing east and walks 20 m east. Turning left from east means north, so she walks 15 m north. Turning right from north means east, so she walks another 25 m east. Turning right from east means south, so she walks 15 m south. The 15 m north and 15 m south cancel, while the eastward distance is 20+25=45 m. She is 45 m from the start, option D.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following number series? 2, 17, 45, 99, 205, ?
questions.explanation: The series is 2, 17, 45, 99, 205, ?. Examine the differences: 17−2=15; 45−17=28; 99−45=54; 205−99=106. Each difference is obtained by doubling the previous difference and subtracting 2: 15→28→54→106. The next difference is 106×2−2=210. Add this to 205: 205+210=415. Option D is correct.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 767, 495, 359, 291, 257, ?
questions.explanation: Find the differences between consecutive terms: 767−495=272; 495−359=136; 359−291=68; 291−257=34. Each difference is half the preceding difference. The next difference is 17, so subtract 17 from 257: 257−17=240. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Find out the number which does not follow the pattern (the odd one) in the given series: 8, 27, 64, 100, 125, 216, 343.
questions.explanation: The numbers 8, 27, 64, 125, 216 and 343 are consecutive perfect cubes: 2³, 3³, 4³, 5³, 6³ and 7³. However, 100 is not a perfect cube and does not fit the pattern. Therefore, 100 is the odd one out, option B.

questions.text: In a 500 meter race, the ratio of the speed of two contestants X and Y is 3:4. Y gives X a head start of 140 meters. Then who will win the race?
options: X will win the race by 20 meters
Y will win the race by 20 meters
X will win the race by 15 meters
Both X and Y will reach the finish line at the same time
questions.explanation: In a 500 m race, X receives a 140 m head start, so X needs to run only 500−140=360 m. Y must run the full 500 m. Their speed ratio X:Y is 3:4. If X's speed is 3 units per second, Y's is 4 units per second. Their times are X: 360/3=120 units; Y: 500/4=125 units. X finishes first. In 120 units of time Y covers 4×120=480 m, leaving 20 m. X wins by 20 m, option A.

questions.text: What is the probability of getting a sum of 9 from two throws of a die?
questions.explanation: Two throws of a fair die produce 6×6=36 equally likely ordered outcomes. The pairs that add to 9 are (3,6), (4,5), (5,4) and (6,3): four outcomes. Probability = favourable outcomes/total outcomes = 4/36=1/9. Option C is correct.

questions.text: A watch gains 5 seconds in 3 minutes and it was set right at 7 a.m. In the afternoon of the same day, when the watch indicated quarter past 4 o'clock, the true time is
questions.explanation: The watch gains 5 seconds for every 180 seconds of true time. Therefore, when the watch shows 185 seconds, only 180 true seconds have passed. From 7:00 a.m. to the indicated 4:15 p.m. is 9 hours 15 minutes = 555 minutes of watch time. True elapsed time = 555×180/185=540 minutes=9 hours. Nine hours after 7:00 a.m. is 4:00 p.m. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Find the number of non-negative integer solutions to the inequality x₁ + x₂ + x₃ + x₄ ≤ 15.
questions.explanation: We need non-negative integer solutions of x₁+x₂+x₃+x₄≤15. Introduce a fifth non-negative integer s=15−(x₁+x₂+x₃+x₄). Then x₁+x₂+x₃+x₄+s=15. By the stars-and-bars formula, the number of non-negative solutions in five variables is C(15+5−1,5−1)=C(19,4)=3,876. Option D is correct.

questions.text: The Maratha and The Kesari were the two main newspapers started by
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak founded and edited the Marathi newspaper Kesari and the English newspaper The Mahratta (also written The Maratha). Both became influential nationalist newspapers during the freedom movement. Lala Lajpat Rai, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Madan Mohan Malaviya were important public figures, but they did not found this pair of newspapers. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first Defence Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Independent India's first Defence Minister was Sardar Baldev Singh, who served in Jawaharlal Nehru's first Cabinet from 1947. K. M. Cariappa later became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army, which is a different office. Sardar Patel was Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister, while Maulana Azad was Education Minister. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Who among the following is the present Education Minister of India?
questions.explanation: The question uses the word “present”, which must be interpreted at the time the paper was set, not as a current-affairs question today. Dharmendra Pradhan became Union Education Minister in July 2021, so he is the intended answer for the paper's stated period. Office-holders can change; do not reuse this as a current 2026 answer without checking the latest Cabinet list. Option D is correct for the paper's context.

questions.text: Mahatma Gandhi founded the ____ newspaper in 1903 in South Africa.
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi started the weekly newspaper Indian Opinion in South Africa in 1903. It was published in English and Indian languages and became an important platform for communicating the concerns of the Indian community and Gandhi's ideas on civil rights. Harijan was a later newspaper associated with Gandhi in India. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following cricketers holds the world record for being the captain of a Test cricket team for the maximum number of matches?
questions.explanation: Graeme Smith of South Africa captained his national Test side in 109 Test matches, more than the other players listed. The question asks specifically about the number of Test matches as captain, not the total number of matches played as a cricketer. Option D is correct.

questions.text: The Sardar Sarovar Project is based on the river
questions.explanation: The Sardar Sarovar Dam and irrigation project is constructed on the Narmada River in Gujarat. The Narmada flows westward into the Arabian Sea and is one of the major rivers of central India. It is not on the Godavari, Tapti or Krishna. Option C is correct.

questions.text: The founder of Boy Scouts and Civil Guides was
questions.explanation: Robert Baden-Powell established the Scout movement. He organised the experimental Scout camp on Brownsea Island in 1907 and published Scouting for Boys in 1908, helping the movement spread internationally. Therefore, the correct option is D, Baden-Powell.

questions.text: Pure water freezes at what temperature?
questions.explanation: At standard atmospheric pressure, pure water freezes at 0°C, which is equivalent to 32°F. The conversion is °F=(9/5×°C)+32; at 0°C this gives 32°F. Option B is correct. The option 0°F is not the freezing point of pure water under standard conditions.

questions.text: Name the Governor General who abolished Sati in 1829.
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck, Governor-General of India, issued the Bengal Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII) in 1829, declaring the practice of sati illegal and punishable. The measure followed reform efforts including those of Raja Ram Mohan Roy. Therefore, option C is correct.

questions.text: Which among the following is the chief ore of aluminium?
questions.explanation: Bauxite is the principal commercial ore of aluminium. Aluminium is extracted from bauxite after refining it to alumina and then using electrolysis to obtain the metal. Cryolite is used in the electrolytic process but is not the chief ore; iron and haematite are associated with iron. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following banks was amalgamated into Punjab National Bank (PNB) during the mega merger of April 2020?
questions.explanation: Oriental Bank of Commerce was amalgamated into Punjab National Bank with effect from 1 April 2020, along with United Bank of India. Allahabad Bank merged with Indian Bank, while Syndicate Bank merged with Canara Bank. Therefore, the correct option is D.

questions.text: Red Cross was founded by
questions.explanation: The Red Cross movement is associated with Swiss humanitarian Henry Dunant. After witnessing the suffering of wounded soldiers at the Battle of Solferino in 1859, he advocated organised voluntary relief for war victims. His efforts helped lead to the founding of the International Committee of the Red Cross in 1863. Option C is correct.

questions.text: The largest part of the human brain is
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain. It is divided into two cerebral hemispheres and is involved in conscious thought, memory, sensory interpretation, language and voluntary movement. The cerebellum coordinates balance and movement, while the midbrain and medulla are smaller brain regions. Option C is correct.

questions.text: The government has launched the Regional Airport Development Programme and part of the Regional Connectivity Scheme of upgrading under-serviced air routes UDAN. What does 'D' stand for in 'UDAN'?
questions.explanation: UDAN is the abbreviation for “Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik”, the Government of India's regional air connectivity scheme. The “D” in UDAN stands for “Desh”. The scheme aims to make air travel more accessible by improving connectivity to underserved and unserved airports. Option D is correct.

questions.text: Who was the first woman Governor of Jharkhand?
questions.explanation: Droupadi Murmu served as the first woman Governor of Jharkhand from 2015 to 2021. She later became the President of India in 2022. Therefore, option D is correct. The question asks about the first woman to hold the governorship, not the first Governor overall.

questions.text: Which Indian pharmaceutical company developed ZyCoV-D, the world's first plasmid DNA vaccine against COVID-19?
questions.explanation: Zydus Cadila (now known as Zydus Lifesciences) developed ZyCoV-D, a plasmid-DNA vaccine against COVID-19. It received emergency-use authorisation in India in 2021 and was notable as the first DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine approved for human use. The other companies listed developed or supplied different vaccines. Option B is correct.

questions.text: How many elements are there in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: The modern periodic table contains 118 elements recognised by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC), from hydrogen (atomic number 1) to oganesson (atomic number 118). The number is based on officially recognised elements, not the number of naturally occurring elements alone. Option D is correct.

questions.text: Which planet has the most number of moons?
questions.explanation: The intended answer in this paper is Saturn. The count of known moons changes as new objects are confirmed, so a question asking which planet has the most moons is time-sensitive. For examination practice, remember the source's intended answer but check a current astronomical source if the question is asked as a present-day fact. Option A is the answer recorded here.

questions.text: First Indian woman to win the Man Booker Prize was
questions.explanation: Arundhati Roy won the 1997 Booker Prize (then called the Man Booker Prize) for her novel The God of Small Things. She was the first Indian woman to receive this award. Kiran Desai later won in 2006, while the other listed writers did not win the prize for this distinction. Option D is correct.

questions.text: Which city is known as the 'Eternal City'?
questions.explanation: Rome is traditionally called the “Eternal City” (Urbs Aeterna), reflecting the ancient Roman idea that the city would endure through time. The title is associated with Rome's long history and importance as the centre of the Roman Empire. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Which planet in the solar system has a blue-green colour?
questions.explanation: Uranus appears blue-green because methane in its upper atmosphere absorbs much of the red light in sunlight, while blue and green wavelengths are scattered or reflected back. This gives the planet its characteristic cyan or blue-green appearance. Pluto, Venus and Mars have different appearances. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Golf player Vijay Singh, who was ranked number 1 for 32 weeks between 2004 and 2005, belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: Vijay Singh is a professional golfer from Fiji. He reached the world number-one ranking and won major championships, representing Fiji internationally. He is not from the United States, India or the United Kingdom. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Fathometer is used to measure
questions.explanation: A fathometer is an instrument used to measure the depth of water, especially the depth of the sea beneath a vessel. It generally works by sending sound pulses downward and measuring the time taken for the echo to return from the seabed. It does not measure earthquakes, rainfall or sound intensity in general. Option C is correct.

questions.text: The developer(s) of Yahoo was/were
questions.explanation: Yahoo was founded by Jerry Yang and David Filo in 1994, initially as a directory of websites created while they were students at Stanford University. Larry Page co-founded Google, while Ray Tomlinson is associated with early network email. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Red dunes, also known as 'theri', which date back to the Quaternary Period, are found in which of the following Indian States?
questions.explanation: Theri are red coastal sand dunes found in Tamil Nadu, particularly in the southern coastal districts. Their red colour is associated with iron-rich minerals in the sand, and they are studied as distinctive Quaternary-age coastal landforms. Among the listed states, Tamil Nadu is correct, option D.

questions.text: Who discovered the sea route to India via the Cape of Good Hope?
questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode) on the Malabar Coast of India in 1498 by sailing from Europe around the Cape of Good Hope. More precisely, Bartolomeu Dias had rounded the Cape earlier; da Gama completed the sea voyage from Europe to India using that route. The question's intended answer is option A.

questions.text: With respect to the 2022 FIFA World Cup, what is Al Rihla?
questions.explanation: Al Rihla was the official match ball used at the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar. Its name means “the journey” in Arabic. It was designed by Adidas for the tournament; it was not the competition's motto, mascot or players' village. Option B is correct.

questions.text: Which was the first online chat system?
questions.explanation: Talkomatic was an early multi-user online chat system developed in 1973 on the PLATO system. It allowed several users to communicate in real time in separate screen areas and is commonly cited as one of the earliest chat rooms. Skype, eBuddy and Google Talk appeared much later. Option D is correct.

questions.text: The line that demarcates the boundary between India and Pakistan is
questions.explanation: The Radcliffe Line is the boundary line drawn during the 1947 Partition to separate the areas that became India and Pakistan (with the Bengal and Punjab boundary awards). The McMahon Line relates to the India–China boundary in the eastern sector, while the Durand Line is between Afghanistan and Pakistan. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Which day is observed as World Population Day?
questions.explanation: World Population Day is observed every year on 11 July. It was established by the United Nations Development Programme in 1989 to draw attention to population issues such as family planning, gender equality, poverty and sustainable development. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Which organization launched a campaign called '#StayHomeIndiaWithBooks' to encourage people to stay home amid the COVID-19 pandemic?
questions.explanation: The National Book Trust, India launched the #StayHomeIndiaWithBooks campaign during the COVID-19 lockdown to encourage reading while people stayed at home. The campaign offered access to selected books and reading resources. Therefore, option A is correct.

questions.text: Which two countries share the longest land border?
questions.explanation: Canada and the United States share the longest international land border in the world, extending for approximately 8,891 kilometres when the Alaska–Canada section is included. The other country pairs listed share shorter borders. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Launched by India's Agriculture Minister Narendra Singh Tomar in 2022, which of the following is the name of a homegrown Indian COVID-19 vaccine for animals?
questions.explanation: Anocovax is an indigenous COVID-19 vaccine developed for animals in India, particularly for protection against SARS-CoV-2 in animals. It was launched in 2022 by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) in the presence of Union Agriculture Minister Narendra Singh Tomar. It is distinct from the human vaccines Corbevax, Covovax and Novavax. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Who worked as Project Director in developing Agni IV and is also known as India's 'Missile Woman'?
questions.explanation: Tessy Thomas is an Indian aerospace scientist associated with the development of the Agni series of ballistic missiles. She served as Project Director for Agni-IV and became popularly known as India's “Missile Woman”. Therefore, option D is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following cities is incorrectly paired with the river that flows through it?
questions.explanation: The question asks for the incorrectly matched city and river. Delhi is associated with the Yamuna, Lucknow with the Gomti, and Tiruchirappalli with the Kaveri. Nagpur is associated with the Nag River and is not situated on the Godavari, so “Nagpur–Godavari” is the incorrect pair. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Announced on 15th September, 2021, AUKUS is a trilateral security pact between which countries?
options: United States, United Kingdom and Ukraine
United States, United Kingdom and Australia
questions.explanation: AUKUS is a trilateral security partnership announced in September 2021 between Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States. The name combines the country initials: AU (Australia), UK (United Kingdom) and US (United States). Ukraine is not a member of this partnership. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Name the organization that has launched the Operation Farishte to prevent trafficking of children.
questions.explanation: Operation Farishtey is an initiative associated with the Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Indian Railways to identify, rescue and protect children found at railway stations and trains, including children vulnerable to trafficking or separation from families. The best option given is Indian Railways (A); the operational role is carried out by the RPF.

questions.text: Who is the present Chief Executive Officer of Apple company?
questions.explanation: For the period relevant to this question, Apple's Chief Executive Officer was Tim Cook, who succeeded Steve Jobs in 2011. Steve Wozniak co-founded Apple, and Steve Jobs was its co-founder and former CEO. The question's use of “present” is time-sensitive; Tim Cook is the intended answer in the source context. Option D is correct.

questions.text: Who is known as the father of Green Revolution in India?
questions.explanation: M. S. Swaminathan is widely known as the father of the Green Revolution in India. His work in agricultural science and the promotion of high-yielding crop varieties, improved farming practices and food-security programmes helped raise India's food-grain production. Verghese Kurien is associated with the White Revolution and dairy development. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of Piedmont Plateau?
questions.explanation: A piedmont plateau lies at the foot of a mountain range and is bounded on its other side by a plain or ocean. The Malwa Plateau is a standard Indian example of this landform; the Tibetan and Bolivian plateaus are intermontane examples, while Ladakh is also associated with high mountain terrain. The National Institute of Open Schooling's geography material lists Malwa as a piedmont plateau. Option C is correct. Source check: NIOS Geography material identifies Malwa as a piedmont plateau.

questions.text: Eight cheetahs were brought from Namibia and released in which National Park of India on 17th September, 2022 to coincide with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday?
questions.explanation: The eight cheetahs brought from Namibia in September 2022 were released at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh. The release took place on 17 September 2022 as part of India's cheetah reintroduction programme. Gir is famous for Asiatic lions, not this cheetah release. Option B is correct.

questions.text: The deficiency of vitamin C causes which of the following diseases?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is needed for collagen formation, healthy connective tissue and wound healing. Severe deficiency causes scurvy, which can produce bleeding gums, poor wound healing, weakness and joint pain. Night blindness is associated with vitamin A deficiency, beriberi with vitamin B1 deficiency, and rickets with vitamin D deficiency. Option C is correct.

questions.text: For galvanizing iron, which of the following metals is used?
questions.explanation: Galvanising iron means coating it with zinc to protect it from rusting. Zinc provides a protective barrier and also corrodes preferentially if the coating is damaged, helping protect the underlying iron. Therefore, zinc is the correct metal, option D.

questions.text: Eugenics is the study of
options: altering human beings by changing their genetic components
questions.explanation: Eugenics is a discredited historical movement and set of practices that sought to influence human heredity by controlling reproduction and selecting supposed desirable traits. Option A is the closest description in the choices. It is important to note that eugenics has been used to justify coercive, discriminatory and abusive policies and is not a valid modern scientific or ethical approach to human worth.

questions.text: National Voters' Day is observed in India on
questions.explanation: National Voters' Day is observed in India on 25 January, the date on which the Election Commission of India was established in 1950. The day aims to encourage voter awareness, registration and participation in elections. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Spain won the title of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022, after defeating which country in the final that was held at the D. Y. Patil Sports Stadium?
questions.explanation: Spain won the 2022 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, defeating Colombia 1–0 in the final at the D. Y. Patil Sports Stadium in Navi Mumbai. The tournament was hosted by India in October 2022. Therefore, Colombia is the correct option, C.

questions.text: To ease the loan process, which of the following States has launched a common credit portal named Simplified Application for Agricultural Loans (SAFAL)?
questions.explanation: Odisha launched the SAFAL portal, meaning Simplified Application for Agricultural Loans, to make agricultural credit applications easier and more accessible. The portal brings participating financial institutions and loan schemes into a common digital application process. Therefore, option A, Odisha, is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following cities is known as the Manchester of South India?
questions.explanation: Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu is popularly called the “Manchester of South India” because of its major textile and cotton-spinning industry. The city developed a strong industrial base supported by cotton-growing regions, mills and related textile businesses. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Who is the founder of the Gupta dynasty?
questions.explanation: Sri Gupta is generally regarded as the founder of the Gupta dynasty, which rose to prominence in northern India in the early centuries CE. Chandragupta I was a later ruler who greatly expanded the dynasty's power and adopted the imperial title Maharajadhiraja. Therefore, option D is correct.

questions.text: What is the time difference between Indian Standard Time and Greenwich Mean Time?
questions.explanation: Indian Standard Time is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), or UTC+05:30. India uses a single standard time based on the 82°30′ east longitude meridian. Therefore, the difference is 5 hours 30 minutes, option C.

questions.text: The value of 4 5/6 + 7 1/2 − 5 8/11 is
questions.explanation: Convert each mixed number into an improper fraction: 4 5/6=29/6, 7 1/2=15/2 and 5 8/11=63/11. The expression becomes 29/6+15/2−63/11. The LCM of 6, 2 and 11 is 66, so this is 319/66+495/66−378/66=436/66=218/33. Converting back to a mixed number gives 6 20/33. Option D is correct.

questions.text: The ratio of the ages of A and B seven years ago was 3:4. The ratio of their ages nine years hence will be 7:8. What is B's present age?
questions.explanation: Let the ages of A and B seven years ago be 3x and 4x respectively. Their present ages are therefore 3x+7 and 4x+7. Nine years from now their ages will be 3x+16 and 4x+16. Using the given ratio: (3x+16)/(4x+16)=7/8. Cross-multiplying gives 24x+128=28x+112, so 4x=16 and x=4. B's present age is 4x+7=16+7=23 years. Option C is correct.

questions.text: An article was bought for ₹5,600. Its price was marked up by 12%. Thereafter it was sold at a discount of 5% on the marked price. What was the amount of discount given?
questions.explanation: First calculate the marked price. A 12% increase on ₹5,600 is ₹5,600×12/100=₹672, so marked price=₹5,600+₹672=₹6,272. The discount is 5% of the marked price: ₹6,272×5/100=₹313.60. Therefore, option B is correct.

questions.text: The average speed of a train is 3 times the average speed of a car. The car covers a distance of 520 km in 8 hours. How much distance will the train cover in 13 hours?
questions.explanation: The car's average speed is distance divided by time: 520÷8=65 km/h. The train's speed is three times the car's speed, so 3×65=195 km/h. In 13 hours the train covers 195×13=2,535 km. Option A is correct.

questions.text: The area of a triangle is half the area of a square. The perimeter of the square is 224 cm. The area of the triangle is
questions.explanation: The square's perimeter is 224 cm. Since a square has four equal sides, each side is 224÷4=56 cm. Its area is 56×56=3,136 cm². The triangle's area is half the square's area, so 3,136÷2=1,568 cm². Option B is correct.

questions.text: The compound interest accrued on an amount of ₹8,500 in 2 years at the rate of 10% p.a. is
questions.explanation: For compound interest compounded annually, amount after two years is P(1+r/100)². Here P=₹8,500 and r=10%. Amount=8,500×1.1²=8,500×1.21=₹10,285. Compound interest=amount−principal=₹10,285−₹8,500=₹1,785. Option B is correct.

questions.text: The average of five consecutive odd numbers is 95. What is the fourth number in descending order?
questions.explanation: Five consecutive odd numbers have a constant difference of 2. Because there are five numbers, their average is the middle (third) number, 95. The sequence in ascending order is 91, 93, 95, 97, 99. In descending order it is 99, 97, 95, 93, 91, so the fourth number is 93. Option D is correct.

questions.text: A and B can finish a work in 18 hours, B and C in 12 hours and A and C in 15 hours. How long will they take to complete the work if they work together?
questions.explanation: Let the one-hour work rates of A, B and C be a, b and c. The question gives a+b=1/18, b+c=1/12 and a+c=1/15. Adding all three equations gives 2(a+b+c)=1/18+1/12+1/15. With denominator 180, the right side is 10/180+15/180+12/180=37/180. Therefore, a+b+c=37/360 of the work per hour. Time for the whole work=1÷(37/360)=360/37 hours=9 27/37 hours. Option D is correct.

questions.text: A train passes a platform 100 m long in 15 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 10 seconds. The speed of the train is
questions.explanation: Let the train's length be L metres and its speed be v metres per second. When it passes a man, it covers its own length in 10 seconds, so v=L/10. When it passes a 100 m platform, it covers L+100 metres in 15 seconds, so v=(L+100)/15. Equating: L/10=(L+100)/15. Thus 15L=10L+1,000, giving L=200 m. Speed=200/10=20 m/s. Convert to km/h: 20×18/5=72 km/h. Option C is correct.

questions.text: Alex sold his radio set at 10% loss. If he had sold it for ₹45 more, he would have made 5% profit. For how much did he sell the radio?
questions.explanation: A 10% loss means the first selling price is 90% of cost price (CP). A 5% profit means the alternative selling price would be 105% of CP. The difference between these selling prices is 15% of CP, and the question says this difference is ₹45. Thus 0.15×CP=45, so CP=₹300. The actual selling price at 10% loss is 90% of ₹300=₹270. Option A is correct.

questions.text: Out of a sum of ₹625, a part was lent at 5% and the other at 10% simple interest. If the interest on the first part after 2 years is equal to the interest on the second part after 4 years, then the second sum is equal to
questions.explanation: Let x be the first amount lent at 5% simple interest and y be the second amount lent at 10%. The interest on the first amount for two years is x×5×2/100=0.10x. The interest on the second for four years is y×10×4/100=0.40y. Since the interests are equal, 0.10x=0.40y, so x=4y. Also x+y=625. Therefore 4y+y=625, 5y=625 and y=₹125. The second sum is option D.

questions.text: A father left a will of ₹16,400 for his two sons aged 17 and 18 years. They must get equal amounts when they are 20 years at 5 percent compound interest. Find the present share of the younger son.
questions.explanation: The younger son is 17, so his share earns compound interest for three years until he is 20. The older son is 18, so his share earns interest for two years. Let the younger son's present share be x; the older son's share is ₹16,400−x. Equal amounts at age 20 give x(1.05)³=(16,400−x)(1.05)². Divide both sides by (1.05)²: 1.05x=16,400−x. Thus 2.05x=16,400 and x=₹8,000. Option A is correct.

questions.text: In a Legislative Assembly, the ratio of the ruling party to the opposition party was 7:3. Due to 18 members leaving the ruling party and joining the opposition party, the ratio was reduced to 3:2. What was the total strength of the Assembly?
questions.explanation: Let the original numbers of ruling and opposition members be 7x and 3x. After 18 members leave the ruling party and join the opposition, the numbers become 7x−18 and 3x+18. The new ratio is 3:2, so (7x−18)/(3x+18)=3/2. Cross-multiply: 14x−36=9x+54, so 5x=90 and x=18. Original total strength=(7x+3x)=10×18=180. Option C is correct.

questions.text: If x² ∝ y³ and x = 3 when y = 5, then the relation between x and y is
questions.explanation: The symbol x²∝y³ means x²=ky³ for some constant k. Substitute x=3 and y=5: 9=k×125, so k=9/125. Hence x²=(9/125)y³. Multiplying both sides by 125 gives 125x²=9y³, or 125x²−9y³=0. Option C is correct.

questions.text: A, B and C enter into a partnership. A contributes one-third of the capital while B contributes as much as A and C together contribute. If the profit at the end of the year amounts to ₹840, what would C receive?
questions.explanation: Let the total capital invested be T. A contributes T/3. B contributes as much as A and C together, so B=A+C. Since A+B+C=T, substitute B: A+(A+C)+C=T, hence 2A+2C=T. With A=T/3, 2T/3+2C=T, so 2C=T/3 and C=T/6. Profit is divided in the ratio of capital, so C receives 1/6 of ₹840=₹140. Option D is correct.

questions.text: The average weight of X, Y and Z is 45 kg, that of X and Y is 40 kg, and of Y and Z is 43 kg. What is the weight of Y?
questions.explanation: The average weight of X, Y and Z is 45 kg, so their total is 3×45=135 kg. The average of X and Y is 40 kg, so X+Y=2×40=80 kg. The average of Y and Z is 43 kg, so Y+Z=2×43=86 kg. Add the last two equations: X+2Y+Z=166. Subtract the total X+Y+Z=135 to obtain Y=31 kg. Option D is correct.

questions.text: The LCM of 2/3 and 4/9 is
questions.explanation: For fractions in lowest terms, the LCM is found by taking the LCM of the numerators and dividing by the HCF of the denominators. The numerators are 2 and 4, whose LCM is 4. The denominators are 3 and 9, whose HCF is 3. Therefore, LCM=4/3. It is also the smallest positive number that is an integer multiple of both 2/3 and 4/9. Option B is correct.

questions.text: The produce of a square field when sold at the rate of ₹1.50 per 100 sq. meters fetches ₹1,350. What will be the cost of putting a fence all around the field at the rate of 50 paise per meter?
questions.explanation: The field's produce earns ₹1.50 for every 100 m². Total revenue is ₹1,350, so the area is (1,350÷1.50)×100=900×100=90,000 m². For a square, side length is the square root of the area: √90,000=300 m. Perimeter=4×300=1,200 m. Fencing costs 50 paise=₹0.50 per metre, so total cost=1,200×₹0.50=₹600. Option C is correct.

questions.text: What is the maximum length of a pencil that can be kept in a rectangular box of dimensions 8 cm × 6 cm × 2 cm?
questions.explanation: The longest straight object that fits inside a rectangular box is its space diagonal, joining two opposite corners. Apply the three-dimensional Pythagorean theorem: diagonal=√(length²+width²+height²)=√(8²+6²+2²)=√(64+36+4)=√104 cm. Therefore, option B is correct.

questions.text: If a cylinder is inscribed in a cube in such a way that the ends of the cylinder are on the opposite faces of the cube, then what is the ratio of the volumes of the cube to the cylinder?
questions.explanation: Let the cube's side be a. The cylinder touches the two opposite faces, so its height is a. Its circular base is inscribed in the square face of the cube, so its diameter is a and its radius is a/2. Cube volume=a³. Cylinder volume=π(a/2)²×a=πa³/4. The ratio cube:cylinder=a³:(πa³/4)=4:π. Option C is correct.

questions.text: A person of height 2 meters wants to get a fruit which is on a pole of height 10/3 meters. If he stands at a distance of 4/√3 meters from the foot of the pole, then the angle at which he should throw the stone so that it hits the fruit is
questions.explanation: The fruit is at the top of a 10/3 m pole, while the person's hand is at a height of 2 m. The vertical distance the stone must rise is 10/3−2=4/3 m. The horizontal distance is 4/√3 m. In the right triangle, tan θ=opposite/adjacent=(4/3)/(4/√3)=√3/3=1/√3. The angle whose tangent is 1/√3 is 30°. Option B is correct.

questions.text: The rainfall (in cm) in a city for the ten-year period 1991–2000 was recorded as follows: 89, 95, 70, 102, 29, 79, 63, 95, 72, 50. The mean rainfall is
questions.explanation: To calculate the mean, add all ten yearly rainfall values: 89+95+70+102+29+79+63+95+72+50=744 cm. Divide by the number of years, 10: mean=744÷10=74.4 cm. This is less than 100 cm, so option C is correct. The question does not require choosing a more precise interval.

questions.text: The equation x² − (2 tan α)x − 1 = 0, where 0° < α < 90°, has
questions.explanation: For a quadratic equation ax²+bx+c=0, the discriminant is Δ=b²−4ac. Here a=1, b=−2tanα and c=−1. Therefore Δ=(−2tanα)²−4(1)(−1)=4tan²α+4. Since tan²α is non-negative for the given range 0°<α<90°, Δ is always positive. A positive discriminant means two real and distinct roots. Option B is correct.

questions.text: If (78)² is subtracted from the square of a number, the answer so obtained is 6460. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Let the required positive number be n. The statement gives n²−78²=6,460. First calculate 78²=6,084. Therefore n²=6,460+6,084=12,544. Since 112²=12,544, n=112. The question asks for the number (normally the positive value), so option A is correct.

questions.text: In an examination, it is required to get 40% of the maximum marks to pass. A student gets 261 marks and is declared failed by 4% marks. What is the maximum marks a student can get?
questions.explanation: The pass requirement is 40% of the maximum marks. The student is short of the pass mark by 4 percentage points, so the student's score is 40%−4%=36% of the maximum. Let the maximum marks be M. Then 0.36M=261, so M=261÷0.36=725. Therefore, the maximum marks are 725, option B. This interpretation treats “fails by 4% marks” as four percentage points below the pass threshold.
